subject: SLA redlines: uptime, credits, and maintenance windows (EtherCloud)
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <e.zhao@ethercloud.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@ethercloud.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EtherCloud redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is aligned on Redwood as our preferred inference partner. Our procurement and SRE teams reviewed the MSA and attached a redline focused on the SLA/support terms. High level asks:

- Uptime target: we need 99.95% for the hosted API used by our customer-facing features (current draft shows 99.9%).
- Service credits: front-load credits for first month if uptime drops below 99.95; we also want clearer tiering (P1/P2/P3).
- Response times: P1 within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours, P3 within 24 hours (business hours basis).
- Maintenance windows: avoid weekly maintenance during our peak window (Mon-Fri 08:00-12:00 PT); propose a single 4-hour maintenance window on Sundays.

I attached the marked-up PDF. Can you confirm which items are deal-breakers for Redwood and where you can be flexible? We have an internal deadline to finalize by end of next week.

Attachments: EtherCloud_MSA_Redlines_2028-07-25.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Director, Procurement | EtherCloud Systems
e.zhao@ethercloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <e.zhao@ethercloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EtherCloud redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Hi Emily — thanks for sending this over and for the quick decision on platform selection. I reviewed the redlines and looped in Legal (Aditya) and Sales (Marissa) so we can coordinate a clean counterproposal.

Preliminary thoughts from Product/Eng: 
- 99.95% uptime is achievable, but it depends on whether EtherCloud will take Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) or use the hosted multi-tenant tier. We can offer 99.95% for Dedicated with a committed baseline; hosted API typically carries 99.9%.
- We'll need to align on the definition of downtime (scheduled vs unscheduled) and how KV/prefix caching behavior affects perceived availability for long-running chat sessions.
- Maintenance: we can commit to avoiding Mon-Fri 08:00-12:00 PT for scheduled maintenance; propose a Sunday 02:00-06:00 PT weekly window as default.

I'm attaching a short note with the product-side constraints and a suggested credit scale. Aditya — can Legal propose language that ties the higher uptime to a capacity commitment? Marissa — can you confirm whether EtherCloud is open to Dedicated or prefers hosted?

Attachments: ava_counter_sla_notes.txt (text, 1 page)

Best,
Ava Chen
Head of Technical Account Management | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <e.zhao@ethercloud.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: EtherCloud redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Team — I reviewed EtherCloud's redlines and Ava's notes. Legal is comfortable with a higher uptime on a conditional basis. Proposed counter language: 

1) Uptime: Redwood will warrant 99.95% monthly uptime for the Services provided under the Dedicated tier, subject to Customer maintaining a minimum committed baseline of X reserved units as set out in the Order Form. For Hosted (non-dedicated) deployments, Redwood's warranty remains 99.9%.

2) Service Credits: A graduated credit schedule based on monthly availability bands (e.g., 99.95 - 99.90: 10% credit; 99.90 - 99.00: 25% credit; <99.00: 50% credit), with a one-time enhanced credit (an additional 10%) available in the first 30 days of service following go-live if availability is below the 99.95 threshold. Credits capped at 100% of monthly recurring charges for the impacted service.

3) Response Times: We accept P1/P2/P3 response windows as follows for Enterprise customers on Dedicated: P1 — acknowledgement within 1 hour and target remediation SLAs to be described in the support playbook; P2 — acknowledgement within 4 business hours; P3 — within 24 business hours. For Hosted customers, response windows remain as per standard support tiers unless upgraded.

4) Maintenance Windows: Redwood will provide a default maintenance window of Sunday 02:00-06:00 PT; Customer may request alternate windows for Dedicated deployments provided there is 14 days' notice. Scheduled maintenance will not be classified as Downtime if notified at least 72 hours in advance and performed within the agreed window.

I'll draft the MSA/Order Form redline wording and send a tracked version. Marissa — can you confirm the committed capacity number we should propose (X) so I can include it in the Order Form?

- Aditya
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <e.zhao@ethercloud.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: EtherCloud redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Hi Emily — appreciate the clear asks and timeline. Quick commercial proposal to unblock procurement: 

- Offer: 99.95% monthly uptime guarantee on the Dedicated plan with a 12-month committed baseline of 10 reserved inference units (this is our shorthand — formal units will be defined in the Order Form).
- Credits per Aditya's draft; first-30-day enhanced credit applies only if customer signs Order Form by 2028-08-05.
- Response times: P1/P2/P3 per Legal's note; we will include the support playbook as an appendix to the Order Form.
- Next steps: I'll circulate a redline Order Form and an accompanying mutual action plan. If you can confirm internal signatories and preferred DocuSign routing, we can target countersignature within 5 business days after countersign.

Related: DocuSign envelope (proposed): https://redwood.app/docusign/eqr-1921
Deal ID: DEAL-ETHER-1921

Emily — any concern with the 12-month commitment? If that's tight, we can propose a 6-month pilot with reduced uptime credits (happy to discuss).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Emily Zhao <e.zhao@ethercloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EtherCloud redlines to MSA + Order Form (SLA section)

Marissa, Ava, Aditya — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the clear counterproposal. EtherCloud is willing to proceed on the Dedicated path with the 12-month committed baseline of 10 units. We reviewed the provisional credit scale and the maintenance language and those are acceptable with two small asks:

1) Add a canary clause allowing a 30-day phased ramp where both parties agree to review performance metrics and credit application for the first production month.
2) Confirm that scheduled maintenance notifications will include an engineering-level available window and post-maintenance validation summary (we'd like to see cache/KV warming notes).

We are ready to sign the term sheet. I've attached a signed term sheet and copied our contracts team for DocuSign routing. We'll route the DocuSign to emily.zhao@ethercloud.com -> contracts@ethercloud.com -> legal@ethercloud.com.

Attachments: Signed_ACME_Termsheet_2028-07-28.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

Next steps: Marissa, can you circulate the tracked Order Form and MSA redline? Aditya — please include the conditional canary clause in the final redline.

Best,
Emily
Director, Procurement | EtherCloud Systems
